candidates.title: Stock tracking rejects a cart quantity above available product or variant stock
candidates.preconditions: One product/variant with stock=1 and stock tracking enabled; start with empty cart.
candidates.fixture: Set tracked product or variant stock to 1, add quantity 1, then request update to quantity 2 and inspect response and cart state.

oracle.observable: With stock tracking enabled and tracking not disabled for the item, attempting to set quantity above product/variant stock returns HTTP 400 with an insufficient-stock message and leaves the prior cart quantity unchanged.

novelty.rationale: Base AddProduct and AddNewProdToCart exercise creation/cart addition but do not assert stock quantity boundary.

baselineOverlap.rationale: Base AddProduct and AddNewProdToCart exercise creation/cart addition but do not assert stock quantity boundary.
baselineOverlap.comparisonBasis: T04-D pinned Gherkin and Java mapping index; structural mapping is not treated as semantic proof.

candidates.negativeControl: With global trackStock disabled or product stock tracking disabled, do not assert this stock-rejection response.
candidates.testabilityRisk: The exact rejection path may depend on cart validation outside the inspected product routes.
candidates.uncertainty: Pinned routes/index.js implements a hard stock bound and separately aggregates quantities held in other carts; cart update UI feedback and configuration/variant edge cases remain unexecuted.
candidates.historicalComparison: Compared with T04-D historical index EC-C01..EC-C05: discount removal, empty cart, product publication admin state, forgotten-password response, and static page create/view. Candidate-specific relation is recorded above; no history entry is overwritten.
candidates.action: Exercise: Product stock boundary prevents or flags an over-stock cart/order.

candidates.title: Customer address update persists and is copied from session into order snapshot
candidates.preconditions: Synthetic customer session with customerPresent/customerId, populated cart, and address fields accepted by the customer update schema; omit address fields from order request to exercise session fallback.
candidates.fixture: Update address through /customer/update, verify database and session values, then create one order with request address fields omitted and compare order snapshot.

oracle.observable: Customer update writes address fields to the customer record and session; a subsequent order creation request that omits address fields falls back to those session values in the persisted order snapshot.

novelty.rationale: Base AddUser is admin user management; it does not cover storefront customer address persistence.

baselineOverlap.rationale: Base AddUser is admin user management; it does not cover storefront customer address persistence.
baselineOverlap.comparisonBasis: T04-D pinned Gherkin and Java mapping index; structural mapping is not treated as semantic proof.

candidates.negativeControl: Use a distinct request-body address and verify the order route prefers the request value over the session fallback.
candidates.testabilityRisk: Session-cached address may mask persistence unless a new session/relogin is used.
candidates.uncertainty: Source shows DB update/session refresh and the order route explicit request-body-or-session fallback. The POST /admin/order/create handler lacks restrict/checkAccess; that auth defect is tracked separately. Runtime flow is NOT_RUN.

candidates.title: Invalid discount date windows are rejected during admin update
candidates.preconditions: An existing synthetic discount code with known start/end values; controlled timezone and application clock.
candidates.fixture: One unique discount record with a future valid window; no real customer data.

oracle.observable: Each invalid update returns the validation error and leaves the stored discount window unchanged.

novelty.rationale: Base discount cases create/use amount and percent codes and include empty/deleted-code paths, but do not assert invalid date-window validation. Historical EC-C01 tests discount removal, a separate behavior. This is a potential gap only.

baselineOverlap.rationale: Base discount cases create/use amount and percent codes and include empty/deleted-code paths, but do not assert invalid date-window validation. Historical EC-C01 tests discount removal, a separate behavior. This is a potential gap only.
baselineOverlap.comparisonBasis: T04-D pinned Gherkin and Java mapping index; structural mapping is not treated as semantic proof.

candidates.negativeControl: Submit a future start and an end later than start; the update should be accepted.
candidates.testabilityRisk: Date parsing and timezone must be controlled; route-level validation can be asserted without relying on redemption behavior.
candidates.uncertainty: Pinned route source checks start-before-now and end-not-after-start on update. It does not establish checkout redemption semantics.
